html: The Nandtaughtacund, also written Nantaughtacund, were an Algonquian people of the middle Rappahannock River in Virginia, around today's Caroline and King George counties. John Smith visited them in 1608 and counted them among the larger groups on the river. They paid tribute to Powhatan's chiefdom and lived by farming maize, fishing and hunting. As the Virginia colony pushed up the river after 1650, they merged with neighbours such as the Rappahannock and disappear from the records.
